subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

options: Texture you can physically feel on the surface
The appearance of texture created on a flat surface
questions.explain: Visual texture is the illusion of texture on a flat surface, whereas actual texture can be touched.

questions.q: Jackson Pollock is famous for which technique?
options: Dripping and pouring paint onto canvas
questions.explain: Jackson Pollock developed a 'drip' technique, pouring paint onto canvas laid on the floor.

questions.q: Which assessment objective involves responding to the work of other artists?
options: Developing ideas through investigation of sources
questions.explain: Developing ideas requires investigating sources, including the work of relevant artists and cultures.

questions.q: The Renaissance saw a renewed interest in...
questions.explain: Renaissance artists revived classical ideals and developed realism and linear perspective.

questions.q: Which artist is closely linked to Impressionism?
questions.explain: Claude Monet was a founder of Impressionism, famous for paintings such as his water lilies.

questions.q: Salvador Dali is associated with which art movement?
questions.explain: Salvador Dali was a leading Surrealist, known for dream-like works such as his melting clocks.

options: Bring together your research and development into your own resolved piece
Be unrelated to your earlier work
questions.explain: A personal response resolves your investigations and development into your own meaningful final outcome.

options: Capturing fleeting light and everyday scenes with loose brushwork
questions.explain: Impressionists used loose, visible brushstrokes to capture changing light and ordinary moments.

questions.q: In GCSE Art, the assessment objective about 'recording' asks you to...
options: Write an essay with no images
Record ideas, observations and insights relevant to your intentions
questions.explain: The recording objective is about capturing observations and ideas, for example through drawing and photography.

questions.q: What does 'tone' refer to in the formal elements?
options: The lightness or darkness of an area
questions.explain: Tone describes how light or dark an area is, helping to create the illusion of form.

questions.q: How are complementary colours defined on the colour wheel?
options: Different tones of the same hue
Colours that sit directly opposite each other
Colours that sit next to each other
questions.explain: Complementary colours are positioned opposite one another on the colour wheel, such as red and green.

options: The dream world and the unconscious mind
questions.explain: Surrealism drew on dreams and the unconscious to create strange, irrational imagery.
